description: His/Met-axial c-type heme of cytochrome c2 (Blastochloris/Rhodopseudomonas viridis), covering ferric (Fe³⁺, low-spin S=1/2) and ferrous (Fe²⁺, low-spin S=0) states. Guberman_HMO_CM5_constpH.name: Ferric His/Met-axial c-type heme (HMO; cyt c2) — CM5
Guberman_HMO_CM5_constpH.methodology:
This is the His/Met-axial c-type heme of cytochrome c2 (Blastochloris viridis), in its oxidized (ferric, Fe3+, net +1), low-spin state - six-coordinate, with a histidine and a methionine bound to iron, and covalently anchored to the protein through the two thioether bonds of the CXXCH motif.

Bonded terms (shared by all four charge sets for this state; the four sets differ ONLY in their charges):
- The porphyrin macrocycle bond/angle/torsion/planarity terms come from the published conste (Henriques 2013) heme model.
- The iron coordination shell (the Fe-N and Fe-S bonds and the angles around iron) is re-fit, separately for the ferric and ferrous states, by the Seminario method - reading the constants off the QM second-derivative matrix (the 'Hessian') of a B3LYP/[LANL2DZ+6-31G(d)] calculation.
- The iron type is forked (FO here; FO ferric / FR ferrous) and the eight beta-pyrrole ring carbons use a custom Cp type (so the heme ring chemistry doesn't collide with nucleic-acid carbons that share the standard name); these let ferric and ferrous parameters coexist in one topology.
- The methionine sulfur-iron twisting term is set to zero on purpose: a QM scan showed that rotation has a negligible barrier and is irrelevant to what this set is for (outer-sphere electrostatics and propionate pKa shifts), so no artificial torsion is imposed.
- Self-contained: the backbone 'stub' residues for the two cysteines, the histidine, the methionine, and the two propionates are bundled in, so only a standard protein force field (ff14SB or ff19SB) need be loaded.

Charges (this set): CM5 (Charge Model 5) - a density-based scheme read directly from the QM electron density, with no fitting. THIS IS THE RECOMMENDED/DEFAULT set. For a buried metal like this heme iron the usual RESP method (which fits charges to the molecule's OUTSIDE electrostatic field) is poorly determined - the outside field barely 'sees' the buried iron - so RESP must pin iron's charge to a separate (Mulliken) estimate, and that pin makes iron's charge change on reduction far too small (about -0.15 of an electron) while pushing the missing charge onto the porphyrin edge. CM5, read straight from the density, gives a clean, conformer-stable picture in which iron's charge changes by about -0.50 of an electron on reduction (the physically expected ~half electron). The trade-off is that CM5 reproduces the external electrostatic field slightly less well than RESP - acceptable for this redox-charge-difference application. The QM link-atom (cap) hydrogens used in the calculation are folded back into their parent atoms so the unit totals exactly its net charge.

References: Henriques 2013 (conste macrocycle; multi-conformer RESP); Seminario 1996 (Fe-shell constants from the QM Hessian); Marenich 2012 (CM5 charges); Bayly-Cieplak-Cornell-Kollman 1993 (two-stage RESP).
